questions.q: What's the difference between trimming and splitting?
questions.a: Trimming shortens a clip's start or end; splitting cuts one clip into two.

days.guide: Shoot the storyboarded scene, each shot twice plus B-roll.

questions.q: What is B-roll?
questions.a: Supplementary footage (details, environment) used for cutaways and transitions.

days.guide: Assemble a rough cut and note missing coverage.

questions.q: What is 'coverage'?
questions.a: The set of shots (angles and sizes) recorded for a scene so it can be edited smoothly.

days.guide: Add dialogue cleanup, room tone and one foley effect; balance levels.

questions.q: Why add room tone under edits?
questions.a: So the background sound doesn't drop out between cuts.

days.guide: Apply color correction and export 1080p.

questions.q: What does 1080p mean?
questions.a: 1920 × 1080 pixel resolution, progressive scan.

weeks.assessment_key: Video draft checklist: all storyboard shots captured (2 takes each) plus 1 minute of B-roll; rough cut follows storyboard; dialogue clear, room tone and one foley effect added; levels balanced; basic color correction consistent; exported 1080p. Proficient = all items complete.

weeks.prep: Clips: Star Wars (1977) main title/Imperial March scenes and Jaws (1975) shark theme; a 2-minute film clip for sound logging; a 30-second silent clip; BandLab.
misconceptions: Students think all film music is background. Some music is diegetic (characters can hear it, e.g., a radio); score is non-diegetic.
Students score every second. Silence can be powerful.
Students ignore sync. Musical hits should land on visual cuts or actions.

days.guide: Listen to Star Wars and Jaws themes and describe how each leitmotif represents a character or threat.

questions.q: How does the Jaws theme create tension?
questions.a: A low, repeated two-note half-step pattern (E–F) that speeds up as the shark approaches.

questions.q: What is a leitmotif?
questions.a: A recurring musical theme associated with a character, place or idea (a technique Wagner made famous).

days.guide: Log sounds in a 2-minute clip as diegetic or non-diegetic.

questions.q: A character turns on a car radio and a song plays. Diegetic or non-diegetic?
questions.a: Diegetic — it exists in the story world.

days.guide: Score a 30-second silent clip twice: suspenseful and comic.

questions.q: Name musical choices that create suspense.
questions.a: Low pitches, minor or dissonant harmony, slow pulse building faster, tremolo strings, silence.

days.guide: Compose a 30–60 second underscore for your scene with a recurring motif.

questions.q: What does 'underscore' mean?
questions.a: Background music beneath dialogue or action that supports mood without dominating.

days.guide: Sync the score to picture and present both versions.

questions.q: What is a 'hit point'?
questions.a: A moment in the picture where the music lines up with an action or cut.

weeks.assessment_key: Scored scene rubric: two contrasting versions (suspense vs. comic) with clear changes in tempo, key/mode and instrumentation; own scene's 30–60 second underscore with a recurring motif; sync points land on cuts; mix balanced under dialogue; presentation explains choices using leitmotif, diegetic/non-diegetic vocabulary.

weeks.prep: Phone, editor, a song (the student's original or a CC-licensed track with attribution), storyboard template, a location plan, and a shooting checklist.
misconceptions: Students cut randomly. Mark beats on the timeline and cut on them; vary pacing between sections.
Students choose copyrighted songs. Use an original or properly licensed track.
Students shoot without a concept. Decide narrative, performance or abstract first.

days.guide: Choose a song and write a concept paragraph.

questions.q: What's the difference between a performance and a narrative music video?
questions.a: Performance shows the artist performing; narrative tells a story with characters.

days.guide: Storyboard 12+ shots mapped to song sections.

questions.q: Why map shots to song sections?
questions.a: So visual energy and changes match the music's structure.

days.guide: Shoot all footage in one session with extra takes.

questions.q: How can you get lip sync to match?
questions.a: Play the song loudly during filming and have the performer sing along with every take.

days.guide: Edit to the beat by marking beats on the timeline.

questions.q: How might pacing differ between verse and chorus?
questions.a: Longer shots in the verse; quicker cuts in the chorus to raise energy.

days.guide: Screen the draft for one viewer and record suggestions.

questions.q: What makes a suggestion actionable?
questions.a: It names a timestamp and a specific change.

weeks.assessment_key: Draft checklist: one-paragraph concept (narrative, performance or abstract); 12+ shot storyboard mapped to song sections; footage including performance and B-roll with extra takes; cuts on the beat with faster pacing in chorus; draft screened with three recorded suggestions.

weeks.prep: Editor, screening setup (TV or laptop), written feedback cards, quiz on film language, sound design and copyright, and a professional music video for comparison.
misconceptions: Students credit only themselves. Credits must include music, collaborators and licenses.
Students revise only visuals. Pacing and sound fixes count.
Students compare with pros by saying 'theirs is better'. Use film vocabulary to identify specific techniques.

days.guide: Apply screening suggestions: fix a pacing issue and a visual issue.

questions.q: Give an example of a pacing fix.
questions.a: Trim a 6-second wide shot to 3 seconds so the chorus starts on the beat.

days.guide: Add a title card and end credits with full attribution.

questions.q: What should end credits include?
questions.a: Cast, crew, music title/artist/license, and any other licensed materials.

days.guide: Host a family screening and collect written feedback.

questions.q: Why use written cards?
questions.a: People are more honest and specific in writing; you keep a record.

days.guide: Give the media arts quiz.

questions.q: Which is non-diegetic: a character's footsteps or the orchestral score?
questions.a: The orchestral score.

days.guide: Write a 300-word comparison of your video and a professional one using film vocabulary.

questions.q: Name two terms to use in your comparison.
questions.a: Shot types/angles, editing rhythm, montage, color grading, diegetic sound, leitmotif.

weeks.assessment_key: Video rubric (each 1–4): Concept, Cinematography (shot variety, angles, composition), Editing (rhythm, continuity, pacing), Sound (sync, levels, score), Credits/ethics (full attribution). Proficient 15+/20. Quiz key: shot types and angles; diegetic vs. non-diegetic; leitmotif; montage; 180-degree rule; foley; room tone; copyright term life + 70; fair-use factors; CC license elements.

weeks.prep: Notebook, mind-map templates, a mood-board tool (paper collage or Canva), and a proposal template with timeline through Week 35.
misconceptions: Students pick projects too big for the time. Scope to what can be finished well in three weeks.
Students skip pre-production. Scripts, storyboards and checklists save time later.
Students choose references without noting techniques. For each reference, name one technique to borrow.

days.guide: Generate three capstone ideas with mind maps.

questions.q: What makes a capstone idea strong?
questions.a: It combines music and media skills, matches your interests, and is achievable in the time.

days.guide: Collect five reference works and note one technique each.

questions.q: Example reference note?
questions.a: 'Song Exploder — uses isolated tracks to explain a song; I'll play stems before the full mix.'

days.guide: Write a 1-page proposal with timeline.

questions.q: Why include a backup plan?
questions.a: Equipment, weather or people may fall through; a backup keeps the project on schedule.

days.guide: Pitch to family in 3 minutes with a mood board.

questions.q: What is a mood board?
questions.a: A collage of images, colors, fonts and references that shows the intended look and feel.

days.guide: Finalize pre-production documents and build a checklist.

questions.q: What's on a shot/recording checklist?
questions.a: Every shot or track needed, location, gear, people and status.

weeks.assessment_key: Proposal rubric: artistic goal, audience, tools and skills, five references each with a borrowed technique, week-by-week timeline (Weeks 33–35), risks and backup plan, pitch delivered in 3 minutes with mood board. Proficient = realistic scope and complete plan.

weeks.prep: BandLab, camera, editor, Audacity; the proposal timeline. Check gear and storage.
misconceptions: Students try to perfect each part before moving on. Get a rough version of everything first.
Students fall behind silently. Compare progress to the timeline at the end of the week.
Students record narration in noisy rooms. Use the closet booth and noise reduction lightly.

days.guide: Compose and record at least 90 seconds of original music in BandLab.

questions.q: How can you build 90 seconds from a short idea?
questions.a: Develop it through repetition, variation, adding layers and contrasting sections.

days.guide: Shoot video or create images following the storyboard.

questions.q: What should you shoot if time allows?
questions.a: Extra takes and B-roll for flexibility in editing.

days.guide: Record narration/vocals and clean with noise reduction.

questions.q: How do you avoid over-processing with noise reduction?
questions.a: Use moderate settings and listen for 'watery' artifacts.

days.guide: Assemble a complete rough cut or rough mix.

questions.q: Why assemble the whole thing roughly?
questions.a: To see structure and timing problems early.

days.guide: Compare progress to the timeline and revise the plan.

questions.q: What should you do if behind schedule?
questions.a: Cut nonessential elements and prioritize the core work.

weeks.assessment_key: Checkpoint: at least 90 seconds of original music recorded; visuals shot/created per storyboard; narration/vocals recorded and cleaned; complete rough cut/mix assembled; updated timeline. Proficient = all present and on schedule (or a realistic revised plan).

weeks.prep: Two viewers for critique, the proposal goals as criteria, editor and DAW, EQ tutorial, artist statement prompt.
misconceptions: Students fix small details first. Address the largest structural issue first.
Students mix music over dialogue. Use EQ and volume to keep voices clear (reduce music in the 1–4 kHz speech range or lower its level).
Students write artist statements that are vague. Name intent, techniques and influences specifically.

days.guide: Show the rough version to two viewers and gather feedback using the proposal goals.

questions.q: Why use your goals as criteria?
questions.a: It focuses feedback on whether the work achieves what you intended.

days.guide: Fix the largest structural issue.

questions.q: Example of a structural issue?
questions.a: The opening is too slow, so the main idea doesn't appear until halfway.

days.guide: Balance music, voice and effects; apply EQ for clear dialogue; export a test mix.

questions.q: What does EQ do?
questions.a: Boosts or cuts specific frequency ranges to shape tone and make room for each sound.

days.guide: Color-correct, add titles, check transitions and graphics.

questions.q: Why check every transition?
questions.a: Glitches or inconsistent transitions distract the audience.

days.guide: Write a 300-word artist statement.

questions.q: What three things should an artist statement explain?
questions.a: Intent, techniques and influences.

weeks.assessment_key: Checkpoint: documented critique against proposal goals; structural revision completed; test mix with clear dialogue; visuals color-corrected and titled; 300-word artist statement (intent, techniques, influences). Proficient = all complete with clear improvement.

weeks.prep: Display setup (screen, speakers, or a web page), audience (family or homeschool group), the capstone rubric, and storage for archive files.
misconceptions: Students read the introduction from a script word-for-word. Use notes and speak to the audience.
Students get defensive in Q&A. Thank the questioner and explain choices.
Students export low-quality archives. Keep full-resolution masters and project files.

days.guide: Plan presentation format, order and introduction.

questions.q: What should a 2-minute introduction include?
questions.a: Title, goal, what to watch/listen for, and a thank-you to collaborators.

days.guide: Present the capstone with a 2-minute introduction.

questions.q: How can you keep the audience engaged?
questions.a: Make eye contact, keep it brief, and tell one behind-the-scenes story.

days.guide: Answer audience questions about process and choices.

questions.q: How do you answer a question you didn't expect?
questions.a: Pause, restate it, answer honestly, and say what you'd explore next.

days.guide: Score the capstone on the rubric and compare with audience feedback.

questions.q: Why compare self-score with audience feedback?
questions.a: It reveals blind spots between intent and impact.

days.guide: Make final fixes and export archive-quality files.

questions.q: What should an archive include?
questions.a: Full-quality exports, project files, stems and assets with licenses.

weeks.assessment_key: Capstone rubric (each 1–4): Concept (clear artistic goal), Craft (technical quality), Music (original, purposeful), Media integration (music and visuals/audio work together), Presentation (2-minute intro, Q&A). Proficient 15+/20. Self-score compared with audience feedback in writing.

weeks.prep: Portfolio site builder (Google Sites, Canva site, or slides), all works from both semesters, the final exam (theory, history, media vocabulary, copyright), reflection prompt. Parent: check privacy settings before sharing links.
misconceptions: Students include every piece. Curate 6–8 of the strongest that show range.
Students omit credits on the portfolio. Each work needs captions and credits.
Students set vague goals. Name a specific skill and course.

days.guide: Select 6–8 best works from both semesters.

questions.q: What criteria should guide selection?
questions.a: Quality, variety across media, and evidence of growth.

days.guide: Build a portfolio site or slide portfolio with captions and credits.

questions.q: What does each caption need?
questions.a: Title, date, medium/tools, a sentence about intent, and credits/licenses.

days.guide: Give the final exam.

questions.q: What are the four fair-use factors?
questions.a: Purpose and character of the use, nature of the work, amount used, and effect on the market.

days.guide: Write a final reflection with evidence from the portfolio.

questions.q: How do you show growth?
questions.a: Compare an early and a late work and describe specific skills that improved.

days.guide: Set goals for next year's arts course and share the portfolio.

questions.q: Write a specific arts goal.
questions.a: 'Learn to read a full vocal score and perform a monologue with music by spring.'

weeks.assessment_key: Final exam key (sample): treble/bass notes; rhythm values; major scale pattern and key signatures; intervals (P4, P5, M3); triads and Roman numerals; I–V–vi–IV; 12-bar blues; Baroque/Classical/Romantic features; swing and call-and-response; gamelan and raga features; rule of thirds; CRAP; shot types and angles; diegetic vs. non-diegetic; fair use factors; CC licenses. Portfolio rubric: 6–8 works with captions and credits, range across music and media, clean layout, working links; reflection cites specific evidence of growth.

WL.overview: Spanish III meets about 50 minutes a day and follows a weekly rhythm: new grammar or vocabulary early in the week, authentic reading/listening and conversation midweek, and a quiz, project, or performance assessment on Friday. Use Spanish for as much of each lesson as you can, model every new structure aloud before practice, and have your child speak and write every day. You do not need to be fluent: rely on the answers given here, SpanishDict or WordReference for conjugations, and recordings of native speakers. Keep a running error log by category (tense, subjunctive, agreement, accents) and reteach any structure scored below 80% before moving on.

weeks.prep: Print a Spanish I–II placement review (present, preterite, ser/estar, gustar) and set up the notebook and Conjuguemos account. Prepare family-tree paper and a phone for recording.
misconceptions: Using estar with personality adjectives (*Mi tía está simpática): personality uses ser — Mi tía es simpática.
Forgetting stem changes or yo-go forms (*yo teno, *ella quere): tengo, quiere.
Saying 'Me llevo bien a mi hermano': the verb is llevarse bien CON — Me llevo bien con mi hermano.

days.guide: Your child takes the placement review without notes, then writes a 10-sentence self-introduction as a baseline. Mark errors by category (verb form, agreement, ser/estar) to plan reteaching.

questions.q: Write a sentence with ser and one with estar about yourself.
questions.a: Example: Soy alto y simpático. Hoy estoy un poco cansado.

days.guide: Review boot verbs (e→ie, o→ue, e→i) and yo-go verbs. Your child drills on Conjuguemos and writes 10 routine sentences.

questions.q: Conjugate preferir for yo and nosotros.
questions.a: prefiero; preferimos

questions.q: Give the yo form of traer, decir, and conocer.
questions.a: traigo, digo, conozco

days.guide: Your child draws a family tree with Spanish kinship terms (el abuelo, la tía, el primo, el sobrino, la cuñada) and describes five relatives' personalities.

questions.q: Translate: 'My cousin is funny and hard-working.'
questions.a: Mi primo es gracioso y trabajador.

questions.q: What is 'el apodo'?
questions.a: A nickname.

days.guide: Your child records a 3-minute interview with 8 questions (¿Qué te gusta hacer los fines de semana? ¿Te llevas bien con tus hermanos?).

questions.q: Ask 'Do you get along well with your siblings?'
questions.a: ¿Te llevas bien con tus hermanos?

days.guide: Give the present-tense quiz and listen to the 1-minute self-introduction, scoring with the checklist.

questions.q: Correct: 'Mi abuela está muy generosa y tene 70 años.'
questions.a: Mi abuela es muy generosa y tiene 70 años.

weeks.assessment_key: Present quiz sample key: querer/ella — quiere; dormir/yo — duermo; pedir/tú — pides; hacer/yo — hago; salir/yo — salgo; conocer/yo — conozco; jugar/ellos — juegan; poder/nosotros — podemos; ir/tú — vas; ser/ustedes — son. Speaking checklist (1-minute self-introduction): name, age, origin, personality (ser + adjectives), likes (gustar), family, routine; 4 = all items, accurate verbs, fluent; 3 = 1–2 items missing or a few errors; 2 = several missing; 1 = minimal.

weeks.prep: Obtain 'Mi nombre' (the 'My Name' vignette from Sandra Cisneros's 'La casa en Mango Street', Spanish translation by Elena Poniatowska) and choose a short Radio Ambulante episode excerpt about identity (Radio Ambulante provides transcripts). Make a ser/estar chart.
misconceptions: Thinking ser = permanent and estar = temporary always: use estar for location (even permanent: Madrid está en España) and ser for events' location (La fiesta es en mi casa).
Using ser for emotions (*Soy orgullosa de...): emotions use estar or sentirse — Estoy orgullosa / Me siento orgullosa de mi herencia.

days.guide: Read 'Mi nombre' aloud together; your child lists five details about the narrator's name and heritage, quoting the text.

questions.q: What does Esperanza say her name means in English and in Spanish?
questions.a: In English it means hope; in Spanish it means too many letters — sadness, waiting.

questions.q: Whom was she named after?
questions.a: Her great-grandmother, who was born in the Chinese year of the horse and spent her life looking out a window.

days.guide: Review ser (identity, origin, characteristics, time, events) vs. estar (location, condition, emotion, progressive). Your child completes 20 sentences.

questions.q: Choose: 'Mi familia ___ de México, pero ahora ___ en California.'
questions.a: es (origin); está (location)

questions.q: Choose: 'Yo ___ nervioso hoy porque el examen ___ a las nueve.'
questions.a: estoy; es

days.guide: Play the Radio Ambulante excerpt twice with the transcript available the second time. Your child answers questions on the speaker's main points.

questions.q: What listening strategy helps with authentic radio?
questions.a: First listen for gist, then reread or relisten for details; use the transcript only to confirm.

days.guide: Your child writes a paragraph about the meaning or story of their own name, modeled on Cisneros.

questions.q: Write a sentence like Cisneros's: 'In English my name means...'
questions.a: Example: En inglés mi nombre significa 'regalo de Dios'; en español suena más suave.

days.guide: Discuss in Spanish: ¿Cómo es la identidad bicultural en California? Your child compares it to their own experience.

questions.q: Translate: 'I feel proud of my heritage.'
questions.a: Me siento orgulloso/a de mi herencia.

weeks.assessment_key: Paragraph rubric ('Mi nombre'): 4 = explains the name's meaning or origin, who chose it, and how the writer feels about it, 8+ sentences, accurate ser/estar and past tenses, vivid detail; 3 = complete with a few errors; 2 = short or many errors; 1 = fragments. Day-1 detail key (from the vignette): in English her name means hope; in Spanish it means too many letters, sadness, waiting; she was named after her great-grandmother, a 'wild horse of a woman' born in the Chinese year of the horse who looked out the window her whole life; at school people say her name as if the syllables were made of tin; she wants a new name like 'Zeze the X'.

weeks.prep: Make a chart of gustar-type verbs (encantar, molestar, importar, interesar, fascinar) and reflexive verbs. Prepare a survey form and a phone for the video. Write the Unit 1 test (present, ser/estar, gustar-type, reflexives, identity vocabulary with reading and listening).
misconceptions: Pronoun mismatch with gustar-type verbs (*A mis padres le importa): plural people take les.
Verb agreement with plural things (*Me molesta los mosquitos): Me molestan los mosquitos.
Leaving off reflexive pronouns in sequences: Me levanto, me ducho y me visto.

days.guide: Model: 'A mi mamá le encanta cocinar. A mis hermanos les molestan las arañas.' Your child writes 10 sentences about family preferences.

questions.q: Translate: 'Politics interests my grandfather.'
questions.a: A mi abuelo le interesa la política.

questions.q: Translate: 'Spiders fascinate me.'
questions.a: Me fascinan las arañas.

days.guide: Your child describes the morning routine with 10 reflexives in order using primero, luego, después, antes de, por último.

questions.q: Translate: 'Before eating breakfast, I get dressed.'
questions.a: Antes de desayunar, me visto.

days.guide: Your child surveys three people (¿Qué te molesta? ¿Qué te interesa?) and reports results in third person.

questions.q: Report: 'Traffic bothers my parents.'
questions.a: A mis padres les molesta el tráfico.

days.guide: Your child records a 2-minute 'Un día en mi vida' video using reflexives and gustar-type verbs.

questions.q: Write a closing line for the video.
questions.a: Example: Y así es un día típico en mi vida. ¡Hasta luego!

days.guide: Give the Unit 1 test.

questions.q: Correct: 'A mi tía le encanta los perros.'
questions.a: A mi tía le encantan los perros.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 1 test sample key: 1) A mi hermano le fascinan los videojuegos 2) Nos importa la familia 3) Me molestan los ruidos 4) Me despierto, me levanto y me cepillo los dientes 5) ser/estar: Somos de Guatemala / Estamos cansados 6) reading/listening items per the texts. Writing scored 4–1 for completeness, accuracy, and variety.

weeks.prep: Make preterite charts: regular endings; irregulars ser/ir (fui), tener (tuve), estar (estuve), hacer (hice), decir (dije, dijeron), poder (pude), poner (puse); spelling changes -car/-gar/-zar (yo) and i→y (leyó, creyeron, oyó).
misconceptions: Writing *dijieron or *trajieron: j-stem verbs drop the i — dijeron, trajeron.
Accent errors: hablé/habló need accents; irregular stems do not (tuve, hizo).
Missing i→y: leer → leyó/leyeron; oír → oyó/oyeron.

days.guide: Review endings; your child writes 8 sentences about last weekend.

questions.q: Translate: 'On Saturday I cleaned my room and watched a movie.'
questions.a: El sábado limpié mi cuarto y vi una película.

days.guide: Drill the irregular stems with quick oral prompts and a written chart.

questions.q: Conjugate decir in the preterite for yo and ellos.
questions.a: dije; dijeron

questions.q: Translate: 'We put the books on the table.'
questions.a: Pusimos los libros en la mesa.

days.guide: Practice spelling changes: busqué, pagué, empecé; leyó, oyeron, creyó, construyeron.

questions.q: Give the yo preterite of sacar, jugar, and comenzar.
questions.a: saqué, jugué, comencé

questions.q: Give the ellos preterite of leer.
questions.a: leyeron

days.guide: Your child writes a 150-word narrative about a memorable trip using 15 preterite verbs, then underlines each.

questions.q: Translate: 'We arrived at the hotel and I fell asleep.'
questions.a: Llegamos al hotel y me dormí.

days.guide: Give the preterite quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Ellos trajieron la comida y yo la servió.'
questions.a: Ellos trajeron la comida y yo la serví.

weeks.assessment_key: Preterite quiz sample key: llegar/yo — llegué; leer/ella — leyó; hacer/él — hizo; decir/ellos — dijeron; poner/yo — puse; poder/tú — pudiste; estar/nosotros — estuvimos; ir/ustedes — fueron; tocar/yo — toqué; creer/ellos — creyeron. Narrative rubric (150 words, 15 preterite verbs): 4 = clear sequence, 15+ correct preterite verbs including irregulars; 3 = 1–3 errors; 2 = many errors or under 120 words; 1 = fragments.

weeks.prep: Gather 3 childhood photos. Make an imperfect chart (regular -aba/-ía; irregular ser, ir, ver). Arrange an interview with a parent or grandparent.
misconceptions: Using the preterite for habits (*De niño, fui a la escuela a pie): repeated past habits use the imperfect — iba.
Missing accents on -ía forms and on -ábamos.

days.guide: Your child learns the forms and writes 8 sentences about childhood habits with siempre, a menudo, todos los días.

questions.q: Translate: 'When I was little, I always went to my grandmother's house.'
questions.a: Cuando era pequeño/a, siempre iba a la casa de mi abuela.

days.guide: Your child describes three photos: where they lived, what they were like, what they used to do.

questions.q: Translate: 'I was shy and I had long hair.'
questions.a: Era tímido/a y tenía el pelo largo.

days.guide: Your child interviews a parent or grandparent with 10 imperfect questions (¿Dónde vivías? ¿A qué escuela ibas? ¿Qué hacías los domingos?).

questions.q: Ask: 'What did you used to do on Sundays?'
questions.a: ¿Qué hacías los domingos?

days.guide: Your child writes a comparison paragraph: 'Mi abuelo jugaba en la calle, pero yo jugaba videojuegos.'

questions.q: Translate: 'My father didn't have a cell phone; I had a tablet.'
questions.a: Mi papá no tenía celular; yo tenía una tableta.

days.guide: Your child presents the interview findings for 2 minutes.

questions.q: Fill in: Mi abuela ___ (ser) muy trabajadora y ___ (ir) al mercado cada día.
questions.a: era; iba

weeks.assessment_key: Interview presentation rubric (2 minutes): 4 = summarizes 6+ facts about the interviewee's childhood in the imperfect (Mi abuela vivía en..., jugaba..., era...) with a comparison to your own; 3 = minor errors; 2 = few facts or mixed tenses; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Draw a timeline graphic: wavy line for ongoing imperfect background, X marks for preterite events. Prepare a 30-item cloze passage (a short story with blanks) and 6-panel comic strips.
misconceptions: Equating English 'was' with the imperfect every time: 'I was sick for a week' (completed) = Estuve enfermo una semana.
Translating 'used to' and 'would (habitual)' with the conditional: habitual 'would' = imperfect (Every summer we would swim = Cada verano nadábamos).
Verbs that change meaning: conocí (I met) vs. conocía (I knew); supe (I found out) vs. sabía (I knew); quise (I tried) vs. quería (I wanted).

days.guide: Explain background (imperfect) vs. events (preterite) with the timeline. Model a short story labeling each verb.

questions.q: Which tense and why: 'It was 8:00 when the movie started'?
questions.a: Eran las ocho (time = imperfect) cuando empezó la película (event = preterite).

days.guide: Your child completes the 30-item cloze passage and writes the reason beside each choice.

questions.q: Choose: 'Yo ___ (leer) cuando mi hermano ___ (entrar).'
questions.a: leía; entró

days.guide: Your child narrates a 6-panel comic using both tenses and connectors (mientras, de repente, entonces).

questions.q: Translate: 'While the kids were playing, it suddenly started to rain.'
questions.a: Mientras los niños jugaban, de repente empezó a llover.

days.guide: Compare English 'was/used to/did' with Spanish aspect; translate 10 sentences and discuss.

questions.q: Translate: 'I knew her' vs. 'I met her.'
questions.a: La conocía. / La conocí.

days.guide: Give the preterite vs. imperfect quiz.

questions.q: Choose: 'Ayer yo (quería/quise) llamarte, pero no (podía/pude).'
questions.a: Context-dependent; most natural: quería llamarte, pero no pude (I wanted to but didn't manage).

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) Eran las diez cuando llegaron — eran (time), llegaron (event) 2) Mientras cocinaba, sonó el teléfono 3) De niño, nadaba todos los días 4) Ayer conocí a tu primo (met) 5) Cuando supe la noticia, lloré 6) Hacía frío y nevaba (description). Score each with the correct reason.

weeks.prep: Find versions of 'La Llorona' and the legend of Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl (learner versions are fine). Preview La Llorona: a ghost story involving the drowning of children. Write the Unit 2 test (preterite, imperfect, the contrast, legends).
misconceptions: Assuming there is one 'correct' version of a legend: legends vary by region; compare versions.
Narrating only in the preterite: legends begin with background in the imperfect (Hace muchos años vivía...).

days.guide: Read La Llorona; your child sequences 6–8 events in Spanish.

questions.q: Summarize La Llorona in one sentence.
questions.a: Una mujer pierde (ahoga) a sus hijos en un río y su espíritu llora y los busca por las noches gritando '¡Ay, mis hijos!'

days.guide: Read the volcanoes legend; your child analyzes its values (love, loyalty, grief).

questions.q: What happens in the legend of Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl?
questions.a: The warrior Popocatépetl goes to war; Iztaccíhuatl is falsely told he died and dies of grief; he returns, carries her body to the mountains, and kneels watching over her with a torch; the gods turn them into volcanoes.

questions.q: What does Iztaccíhuatl's shape resemble?
questions.a: A sleeping woman (it is called 'la mujer dormida').

days.guide: Discuss in Spanish what each legend teaches and why it endures.

questions.q: Why might parents have told La Llorona to children?
questions.a: To warn them not to go near rivers or wander at night, and to teach about the consequences of actions.

days.guide: Your child writes a 250-word original legend explaining a local landmark.

questions.q: Write an opening line for a legend.
questions.a: Example: Hace muchos siglos, cuando no había ciudades en este valle, vivía un joven muy valiente...

days.guide: Your child records the legend aloud; then give the Unit 2 test.

questions.q: Fill in: Los dioses ___ (convertir) a los enamorados en volcanes.
questions.a: convirtieron

weeks.assessment_key: Legend writing rubric (250 words): 4 = clear explanation of a local landmark, imperfect for setting and preterite for events, a lesson or moral, few errors; 3 = minor errors; 2 = weak structure or many errors; 1 = incomplete. Unit 2 test sample: 1) La Llorona busca a sus hijos 2) Popocatépetl was the warrior who watches over the sleeping Iztaccíhuatl 3) tense items with reasons.

weeks.prep: Bookmark Spanish versions of airline and hotel websites (Iberia, Aeroméxico, Booking.com in Spanish). Make flashcards: la aduana, facturar el equipaje, el boleto de ida y vuelta, la tarjeta de embarque, el asiento de ventanilla/pasillo, el alojamiento.
misconceptions: Translating 'to check (a bag)' as 'chequear': use facturar (Spain/Latin America) or documentar (Mexico) el equipaje.
Confusing 'el boleto de ida' (one-way) and 'de ida y vuelta' (round-trip).

days.guide: Your child learns the vocabulary with flashcards and a matching game.

questions.q: What is 'la aduana'?
questions.a: Customs (at the border/airport).

days.guide: Your child navigates a Spanish-language airline or hotel site and records prices, times, and policies.

questions.q: What does 'tarifa' mean on a booking site?
questions.a: Fare/rate (price).

days.guide: Role-play: you are the airline agent and hotel receptionist. Your child checks in, requests a window seat, and asks about breakfast.

questions.q: Ask: 'Is breakfast included?'
questions.a: ¿Está incluido el desayuno?

questions.q: Ask for a window seat.
questions.a: Quisiera un asiento de ventanilla, por favor.

days.guide: Your child creates a 5-day itinerary for a chosen country with transport and lodging.

questions.q: Translate: 'On Tuesday we will take a train to Seville.'
questions.a: El martes tomaremos un tren a Sevilla.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz and the role-play assessment.

questions.q: Translate: 'I have to check two suitcases.'
questions.a: Tengo que facturar dos maletas.

weeks.assessment_key: Vocabulary quiz sample key: la aduana = customs; facturar = to check (luggage); el boleto de ida y vuelta = round-trip ticket; la tarjeta de embarque = boarding pass; el alojamiento = lodging; la habitación doble = double room; el vuelo directo = direct flight. Role-play rubric: 4 = checks in at airport and hotel, asks 3+ questions politely with usted, understands responses; 3 = minor errors; 2 = needs prompting; 1 = cannot complete.

weeks.prep: Chart future endings (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án on the infinitive) and irregular stems (tendr-, saldr-, pondr-, vendr-, podr-, sabr-, querr-, habr-, har-, dir-).
misconceptions: Using the future for immediate plans only: in conversation ir a + infinitive is more common for near plans; the future also expresses probability (¿Qué hora será? = I wonder what time it is).
Regularizing irregular stems (*saliré): saldré.

days.guide: Your child learns the regular future and writes 10 predictions for the trip.

questions.q: Translate: 'We will visit three museums.'
questions.a: Visitaremos tres museos.

days.guide: Drill irregular stems with a card game.

questions.q: Conjugate hacer and decir in the future for yo.
questions.a: haré; diré

questions.q: Translate: 'There will be many people.'
questions.a: Habrá mucha gente.

days.guide: Compare ir a + infinitive and the future; your child rewrites 10 sentences each way.

questions.q: Rewrite with the future: 'Voy a salir a las ocho.'
questions.a: Saldré a las ocho.

days.guide: Your child writes 10 predictions about life in 2050.

questions.q: Translate: 'In 2050 cars will drive themselves.'
questions.a: En 2050 los carros se manejarán solos (or los coches conducirán solos).

days.guide: Give the future quiz.

questions.q: What does '¿Qué hora será?' mean?
questions.a: 'I wonder what time it is' (future of probability).

weeks.assessment_key: Future quiz sample key: viajar/yo — viajaré; tener/tú — tendrás; salir/ella — saldrá; hacer/nosotros — haremos; decir/ellos — dirán; poder/yo — podré; saber/ustedes — sabrán; venir/tú — vendrás; haber (there will be) — habrá; probability: '¿Dónde estará Juan?' = I wonder where Juan is.

weeks.prep: Bookmark UNESCO World Heritage pages in Spanish (whc.unesco.org/es) and national tourism sites. Prepare brochure paper or a template.
misconceptions: Copying text from websites into the brochure: write original Spanish and cite sources.
Assuming Spanish-speaking countries have uniform climates: altitude and hemisphere matter (Quito is mild year-round; Patagonia is cold).

days.guide: Your child researches a UNESCO site (e.g., la Alhambra, Machu Picchu, Chichén Itzá, el centro histórico de Cartagena) and records 5 facts in Spanish.

questions.q: Where is the Alhambra and who built it?
questions.a: Granada, Spain; built mainly by the Nasrid dynasty (Muslim rulers) in the 13th–14th centuries.

questions.q: Where is Chichén Itzá?
questions.a: On the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico — a Maya city.

days.guide: Your child compares the site's climate and geography with California.

questions.q: Translate: 'Cusco is colder than Los Angeles because it is in the mountains.'
questions.a: Cusco es más frío que Los Ángeles porque está en las montañas.

days.guide: Your child researches two regional dishes and their ingredients.

questions.q: Name a dish from Colombia and its main ingredient.
questions.a: Example: la arepa — harina de maíz (corn flour); or la bandeja paisa — beans, rice, meat, egg, plantain, avocado.

days.guide: Your child designs the brochure with formal commands (¡Visite...! ¡Pruebe...!).

questions.q: Write a usted command: 'Try the ceviche!'
questions.a: ¡Pruebe el ceviche!

days.guide: Your child presents the brochure for 3 minutes.

questions.q: Translate: 'You will see the most beautiful beaches.'
questions.a: Verá las playas más bonitas.

weeks.assessment_key: Brochure and presentation rubric: 4 = accurate facts on a UNESCO site, climate/geography compared with California, two regional dishes with ingredients, attractive layout, 3-minute presentation with future and commands (Visite..., Pruebe...); 3 = minor gaps; 2 = missing a section or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Make role-play cards (lost luggage, missed flight, hotel complaint) and a Madrid city map. Chart formal commands (usted/ustedes) including irregulars (vaya, sea, esté, dé, sepa) and spelling changes (busque, llegue, empiece). Write the Unit 3 test (travel vocabulary, future, formal commands).
misconceptions: Using tú forms with hotel staff or strangers: use usted commands and polite phrases (¿Podría...?).
Putting pronouns before affirmative commands (*Me ayude): attach them — Ayúdeme; negative: No me ayude.

days.guide: Act out the three scenarios; your child explains the problem and asks for help politely.

questions.q: Say: 'My suitcase didn't arrive.'
questions.a: Mi maleta no llegó.

questions.q: Say: 'I missed my flight.'
questions.a: Perdí mi vuelo.

days.guide: Teach Ud./Uds. commands from the yo form; your child conjugates 15 verbs.

questions.q: Give usted commands for cruzar, seguir, and ir.
questions.a: cruce, siga, vaya

days.guide: Give directions on the Madrid map using commands (Salga del hotel, doble a la derecha, siga por la Gran Vía...).

questions.q: Translate: 'Cross the plaza and turn right.'
questions.a: Cruce la plaza y doble a la derecha.

days.guide: Your child writes a formal complaint email to a hotel (greeting, problem, request, closing).

questions.q: Give a formal greeting and closing for an email.
questions.a: Estimado/a señor/a: ... Atentamente, (nombre)

days.guide: Give the Unit 3 test.

questions.q: Make negative with the pronoun: 'Llámeme.'
questions.a: No me llame.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 3 test sample key: 1) Siga derecho y doble a la izquierda 2) usted commands: vaya, tenga, haga, sea, busque 3) future: tendremos, saldré 4) la maleta perdida = lost suitcase; el retraso = delay; quejarse = to complain. Complaint email scored 4–1 on formal register (Estimado/a..., Atentamente), clear problem and request, accuracy.

weeks.prep: Gather Spanish pharmacy ads (Farmacias Similares, Farmacias del Ahorro websites) and body vocabulary flashcards.
misconceptions: Using possessives with body parts (*Me duele mi garganta): Me duele la garganta.
Confusing 'la receta' meanings: it means both a recipe and a prescription; context decides.

days.guide: Your child learns body and illness vocabulary and practices doler with all pronouns.

questions.q: Translate: 'His back hurts.'
questions.a: Le duele la espalda.

days.guide: Role-play a doctor's visit; you ask ¿Qué síntomas tiene? ¿Desde cuándo?

questions.q: Answer: 'I've had a fever since Monday.'
questions.a: Tengo fiebre desde el lunes.

days.guide: Your child reads pharmacy ads and medicine instructions and explains dosages in English.

questions.q: What does 'Tome una tableta cada doce horas' mean?
questions.a: Take one tablet every twelve hours.

days.guide: Your child writes a diary entry about a time they were sick using preterite and imperfect.

questions.q: Translate: 'I was sick for three days and I couldn't go out.'
questions.a: Estuve enfermo/a tres días y no pude salir.

days.guide: Give the quiz and the role-play assessment.

questions.q: Correct: 'Me duelen la cabeza.'
questions.a: Me duele la cabeza.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: la fiebre = fever; toser = to cough; estornudar = to sneeze; la receta = prescription; Me duelen los oídos = My ears hurt; tener escalofríos = to have chills; estar mareado/a = to be dizzy. Role-play scored 4–1 on symptoms described accurately with doler/tener/estar and appropriate questions.

weeks.prep: Chart tú commands: affirmative = él form (habla, come); irregulars di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven; negative = no + subjunctive (no hables, no comas, no vayas). Prepare poster paper.
misconceptions: Using the affirmative form in negatives (*No come): No comas.
Forgetting the accent when attaching pronouns: Dímelo, Hazlo (one-syllable + one pronoun needs no accent), Cómelo.
Confusing 've' (go, from ir) and 've' (see, from ver): context decides; 'sé' (be) has an accent.

days.guide: Teach affirmative tú commands and the 8 irregulars with a chant. Your child gives commands to you and you obey.

questions.q: Give affirmative tú commands for salir, tener, and ser.
questions.a: sal, ten, sé

days.guide: Teach negatives from the yo form; your child writes 10 negative commands.

questions.q: Translate: 'Don't eat so much sugar.'
questions.a: No comas tanto azúcar.

questions.q: Translate: 'Don't go to bed late.'
questions.a: No te acuestes tarde.

days.guide: Practice pronoun placement: attached to affirmatives, before negatives.

questions.q: Rewrite with a pronoun: 'Bebe el agua.' and its negative.
questions.a: Bébela. / No la bebas.

questions.q: Rewrite: 'Dime la verdad' as negative.
questions.a: No me digas la verdad.

days.guide: Your child creates a health-advice poster with 10 commands.

questions.q: Write: 'Sleep eight hours.'
questions.a: Duerme ocho horas.

days.guide: Give the commands quiz.

questions.q: Make negative: 'Hazlo ahora.'
questions.a: No lo hagas ahora.

weeks.assessment_key: Commands quiz sample key: 1) decir — di / no digas 2) hacer — haz / no hagas 3) ir — ve / no vayas 4) ser — sé / no seas 5) poner — pon / no pongas 6) comer + lo — cómelo / no lo comas 7) acostarse — acuéstate / no te acuestes 8) tener — ten / no tengas. Poster rubric: 4 = 10 accurate commands with health advice and visuals; 3 = 1–2 errors; 2 = several errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find an article on Cuba's or Mexico's health system and a text on herbal remedies (té de manzanilla, sábila/aloe, té de jengibre). Write the Unit 4 test (health vocabulary, commands, cultural comparisons).
misconceptions: Presenting traditional remedies as replacements for medical care: they are cultural practices; serious illness needs a doctor.
Generalizing that all people in a country use curanderos: practices vary by region and family.

days.guide: Your child reads the article and summarizes main points in Spanish.

questions.q: Summarize Cuba's system in one Spanish sentence.
questions.a: En Cuba, el gobierno ofrece atención médica gratuita y universal, con muchos médicos de familia.

days.guide: Your child learns about remedies and the perspectives behind them (trust in nature, family knowledge).

questions.q: What is sábila traditionally used for?
questions.a: Aloe vera — applied to burns and skin irritations.

days.guide: Your child creates a Venn diagram comparing two countries and the U.S.

questions.q: Write a comparison sentence.
questions.a: Example: En Estados Unidos muchas personas necesitan seguro médico privado, pero en Cuba la atención es gratuita.

days.guide: Discuss pros and cons of each system in Spanish.

questions.q: Give a pro and a con of a public system in Spanish.
questions.a: Ventaja: todos tienen acceso. Desventaja: a veces hay que esperar mucho o faltan recursos.

days.guide: Give the Unit 4 test.

questions.q: What is 'el curandero'?
questions.a: A traditional healer who uses herbs and remedies.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 4 test sample key: 1) el curandero = traditional healer 2) el seguro médico = health insurance 3) la sábila (aloe vera) se usa para quemaduras 4) commands: Descansa, No comas grasa, Tome la medicina 5) cultural comparison: Cuba has a universal, state-run system; Mexico has public institutions (IMSS, ISSSTE) plus private care; the U.S. relies on private insurance plus Medicare/Medicaid. Discussion rubric: 4 = sustains discussion with pros/cons and supporting reasons.

weeks.prep: Gather Spanish infographics on the environment (UN, WWF en español) and a Spanish PSA video. Prepare vocabulary cards.
misconceptions: Confusing 'la contaminación' (pollution) with 'contamination' only: it covers air, water, and soil pollution.
Thinking all of Chile is rainy or all dry: Chile's 'megasequía' (megadrought) has affected central Chile since about 2010.

days.guide: Your child labels infographics with new vocabulary.

questions.q: Translate: 'Recycling reduces trash.'
questions.a: El reciclaje reduce la basura.

days.guide: Read about Amazon deforestation and Chile's drought; your child lists causes and effects.

questions.q: Name a cause of Amazon deforestation.
questions.a: La ganadería (cattle ranching), la agricultura (soy), la tala ilegal (illegal logging), la minería.

days.guide: Watch the PSA; your child summarizes it in 5 Spanish sentences.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a PSA (anuncio de servicio público)?
questions.a: To inform the public and persuade people to change a behavior for the common good.

days.guide: Your child describes three environmental problems in their community.

questions.q: Translate: 'In my city there is a lot of traffic and air pollution.'
questions.a: En mi ciudad hay mucho tráfico y contaminación del aire.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz.

questions.q: What does 'la sequía' mean?
questions.a: Drought.

weeks.assessment_key: Vocabulary quiz sample key: la contaminación = pollution; el reciclaje = recycling; la deforestación = deforestation; la sequía = drought; los recursos naturales = natural resources; el calentamiento global = global warming; ahorrar = to save; desperdiciar = to waste; la capa de ozono = ozone layer; las energías renovables = renewable energy.

weeks.prep: Make the subjunctive formation chart (yo, drop -o, opposite vowel) and DISHES irregulars: dar (dé), ir (vaya), ser (sea), haber (haya), estar (esté), saber (sepa).
misconceptions: No change of subject: 'Quiero reciclar' (infinitive) vs. 'Quiero que reciclemos' (subjunctive).
Using indicative after recommendations (*Recomiendo que usas): use uses.
Spelling changes: buscar → busque, llegar → llegue, proteger → proteja.

days.guide: Teach formation from the yo form; your child conjugates 15 verbs.

questions.q: Give the subjunctive of hacer (yo), poner (tú), and conocer (ellos).
questions.a: haga, pongas, conozcan

days.guide: Memorize DISHES irregulars with a mnemonic.

questions.q: Give the subjunctive yo forms of dar, ir, and saber.
questions.a: dé, vaya, sepa

days.guide: Your child writes 10 sentences with querer que, recomendar que, pedir que.

questions.q: Translate: 'My mom asks me to turn off the lights.'
questions.a: Mi mamá me pide que apague las luces.

days.guide: Your child writes environmental advice with es importante/necesario que.

questions.q: Translate: 'It's necessary that people use less plastic.'
questions.a: Es necesario que la gente use menos plástico.

days.guide: Give the subjunctive quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Quiero que tú vas conmigo.'
questions.a: Quiero que tú vayas conmigo.

weeks.assessment_key: Subjunctive quiz sample key: hablar/yo — hable; tener/tú — tengas; ir/nosotros — vayamos; ser/ellos — sean; dar/él — dé; saber/ustedes — sepan; estar/yo — esté; haber — haya; 'I want you to recycle' — Quiero que (tú) recicles; 'It's important that we protect the forests' — Es importante que protejamos los bosques.

weeks.prep: Find an article on Costa Rica's renewable energy (it generates about 98–99% of its electricity from renewables — hydro, geothermal, wind, solar — in most years) and ecotourism. Prepare debate prompts and a recording device.
misconceptions: Saying Costa Rica uses only renewable energy for everything: its electricity is nearly all renewable, but transportation still relies heavily on fossil fuels.
Using the indicative in recommendations to the mayor: Le recomiendo que construya..., Es urgente que la ciudad ahorre...

days.guide: Your child reads about Costa Rica and summarizes its strategies.

questions.q: Where does most of Costa Rica's electricity come from?
questions.a: Renewable sources, mainly hydroelectric power, plus geothermal, wind, and solar.

days.guide: Hold a debate in Spanish on the best solution for California drought (conservation, desalination, recycled water).

questions.q: Give an opinion with a reason.
questions.a: Example: Creo que es mejor reciclar el agua porque cuesta menos que desalinizarla.

days.guide: Your child writes a letter to a mayor with 8 subjunctive recommendations.

questions.q: Translate: 'I recommend that the city plant more trees.'
questions.a: Le recomiendo que la ciudad plante más árboles.

days.guide: Your child records a 1-minute environmental PSA.

questions.q: Write a slogan.
questions.a: Example: ¡Ahorra agua hoy para tener agua mañana!

days.guide: Your child presents the PSA; score with the rubric.

questions.q: Fill in: Es urgente que nosotros ___ (cuidar) el agua.
questions.a: cuidemos

weeks.assessment_key: PSA rubric: 4 = 1 minute, clear message, 4+ subjunctive/command structures, accurate vocabulary, engaging delivery; 3 = minor errors; 2 = unclear or many errors; 1 = incomplete. Letter: 8 recommendations with correct subjunctive (Le recomiendo que la ciudad instale paneles solares...).

weeks.prep: Assemble a review packet (present, preterite, imperfect, future, commands, present subjunctive) and the semester exam with reading, listening, and writing. Print ACTFL can-do statements.
misconceptions: Choosing tenses by English translation alone: decide by function (background vs. event, habit vs. single action).
Forgetting that commands and the subjunctive share forms (No comas / Quiero que comas).

days.guide: Your child completes a mixed tense exercise and corrects errors.

questions.q: Give: imperfect nosotros of ir, preterite ella of poder, future yo of venir.
questions.a: íbamos, pudo, vendré

days.guide: Review subjunctive and commands with a mixed set.

questions.q: Translate: 'Don't tell me' and 'I want you to tell me.'
questions.a: No me digas. / Quiero que me digas.

days.guide: Hold a 5-minute conversation on semester themes (identity, childhood, travel, health, environment).

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué recomiendas para proteger el medio ambiente?'
questions.a: Example: Recomiendo que usemos transporte público y que reciclemos más.

days.guide: Give the semester exam (reading, listening, writing).

questions.q: Fill in: Cuando yo ___ (tener) diez años, ___ (viajar) a España por primera vez.
questions.a: tenía; viajé

days.guide: Your child self-assesses with can-do statements and sets goals.

questions.q: Write a goal with the future: 'I will speak more Spanish at home.'
questions.a: Hablaré más español en casa.

weeks.assessment_key: Semester exam: grammar items sample — fui, iba, saldré, hagas, vayamos, Hazlo, No lo hagas; reading and listening keys per the chosen texts; writing scored 4–1 for task completion, accuracy, and organization. Oral interview rubric: 4 = 5 minutes sustained, uses multiple tenses accurately, asks questions; 3 = minor errors; 2 = short answers; 1 = cannot sustain.

weeks.prep: Open high-resolution images of Velázquez's Las Meninas (Museo del Prado), a Frida Kahlo self-portrait (e.g., Autorretrato con collar de espinas y colibrí), Diego Rivera murals, Chicano murals in San Francisco's Mission District (Balmy Alley, the Women's Building) and Los Angeles (Judy Baca's Great Wall of Los Angeles), and Picasso's Guernica (Museo Reina Sofía). Preview: Guernica shows wartime death and suffering; Kahlo's work depicts pain and injury.
misconceptions: Using 'en el fondo' and 'al fondo' loosely: al fondo = in the background (location in the picture); en el fondo = deep down/basically.
Describing paintings only with 'es': use hay (there is), está/están (location), se ve/se ven (one sees), and representa/simboliza for meaning.
Thinking Guernica shows a battle between armies: it depicts the 1937 aerial bombing of a civilian town.

days.guide: Teach art vocabulary (el cuadro, el autorretrato, el primer plano, al fondo, a la izquierda/derecha, representar). Display Las Meninas; your child writes 6 sentences describing who and what appears where.

questions.q: Who is the girl at the center of Las Meninas, and who are 'las meninas'?
questions.a: The Infanta Margarita Teresa (daughter of King Philip IV); the meninas are her maids of honor attending her.

questions.q: Where do the king and queen appear in the painting?
questions.a: Reflected in the mirror at the back (al fondo) of the room; Velázquez himself stands at a large canvas on the left.

days.guide: Read a short Spanish biography of Frida Kahlo together. Your child analyzes one self-portrait: symbols, colors, expression, and what it says about identity.

questions.q: What event shaped Frida Kahlo's life and art when she was 18?
questions.a: A bus accident (1925) that badly injured her spine and pelvis; she began painting while recovering and lived with pain all her life.

questions.q: Translate: 'In her self-portraits she wears traditional Mexican clothing.'
questions.a: En sus autorretratos ella lleva ropa tradicional mexicana.

days.guide: Show Diego Rivera murals and Chicano murals in the Mission District and Los Angeles. Discuss in Spanish why murals are public art and whom they speak to.

questions.q: Why did Mexican muralists like Rivera paint on public walls?
questions.a: To teach history and celebrate workers and Indigenous people to everyone, including people who could not read, after the Mexican Revolution.

questions.q: Name a famous Chicano mural project in Los Angeles.
questions.a: The Great Wall of Los Angeles, directed by Judy Baca, a half-mile mural of California history.

days.guide: Your child studies Guernica and its context, then identifies at least four symbols and offers interpretations in Spanish.

questions.q: What happened at Guernica in 1937?
questions.a: During the Spanish Civil War, German (and Italian) planes supporting Franco bombed the Basque town of Guernica on April 26, 1937, killing many civilians.

questions.q: Why is the painting in black, white, and gray?
questions.a: Possible answer: it looks like a newspaper photo and expresses death, mourning, and horror without the distraction of color.

days.guide: Your child writes a museum label for one artwork and reads it aloud as a docent would.

questions.q: Translate: 'In the background one sees a mirror.'
questions.a: Al fondo se ve un espejo.

weeks.assessment_key: Museum label rubric (60–100 words): 4 = title, artist, date, medium, museum; accurate description using hay/se ve/representa; one sentence of historical context and one of interpretation; correct agreement; 3 = one element missing or a few errors; 2 = mostly description with errors; 1 = incomplete. Model label: 'Guernica (1937), Pablo Picasso. Óleo sobre lienzo. Museo Reina Sofía, Madrid. Picasso pintó este mural después del bombardeo de la ciudad vasca de Guernica durante la Guerra Civil española. En el cuadro se ven un toro, un caballo herido y una madre que grita con su hijo muerto. Los colores grises, negros y blancos representan el dolor y el horror de la guerra.'

weeks.prep: Chart the present perfect: haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) + participle (-ado/-ido). List irregular participles: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, roto, vuelto, abierto, muerto, cubierto, descubierto, resuelto. Note accent participles: leído, oído, creído, traído.
misconceptions: Separating haber from the participle or putting pronouns between them (*He lo visto): pronouns go before haber — Lo he visto.
Making the participle agree after haber (*Ella ha comida): with haber it never changes — Ella ha comido.
Using tener as the helper (*Tengo comido): only haber forms the perfect tense.

days.guide: Teach the formation with regular participles. Your child writes 10 sentences about things done this week (Esta semana he limpiado...).

questions.q: Translate: 'We have studied a lot this year.'
questions.a: Hemos estudiado mucho este año.

questions.q: Give the participle of leer and of vivir.
questions.a: leído; vivido

days.guide: Drill the irregular participles with flashcards and a quick oral game.

questions.q: Give the participles of hacer, decir, escribir, ver, poner, romper, and volver.
questions.a: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, roto, vuelto

questions.q: Translate: 'Who has broken the window?'
questions.a: ¿Quién ha roto la ventana?

days.guide: Your child interviews you or a relative with 8 '¿Alguna vez has...?' questions and notes the answers in third person.

questions.q: Ask: 'Have you ever eaten paella?'
questions.a: ¿Alguna vez has comido paella?

questions.q: Report the answer: 'She has never seen the ocean.'
questions.a: Ella nunca ha visto el mar.

days.guide: Your child writes a bucket list: 8 things they have done (ya) and 8 they haven't done yet (todavía no).

questions.q: Translate: 'I have already flown on a plane, but I haven't visited Spain yet.'
questions.a: Ya he volado en avión, pero todavía no he visitado España.

days.guide: Give the present-perfect quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Mis padres han hacido la cena y yo he lo comido.'
questions.a: Mis padres han hecho la cena y yo la he comido.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) hablar/yo — he hablado 2) comer/tú — has comido 3) hacer/ella — ha hecho 4) decir/nosotros — hemos dicho 5) escribir/ellos — han escrito 6) ver/ustedes — han visto 7) poner/yo — he puesto 8) romper/él — ha roto 9) volver/tú — has vuelto 10) abrir/nosotros — hemos abierto 11) 'Have you ever been to Mexico?' — ¿Alguna vez has estado en México? 12) 'I haven't finished yet' — Todavía no he terminado.

weeks.prep: Locate José Martí's 'Yo soy un hombre sincero' (Versos sencillos I, public domain), Pablo Neruda's 'Oda al tomate' (Odas elementales; use a library or licensed copy), and a Gabriela Mistral poem (e.g., from Ternura). Preview a sung version of 'Guantanamera', which uses lines from Martí.
misconceptions: Counting syllables like English: Spanish meter counts syllables with sinalefa (vowels across words join) — Martí's lines are octosyllabic (8 syllables).
Confusing metaphor and simile: a simile uses como; a metaphor states it directly.
Reading poems line by line as separate sentences: follow punctuation across lines (encabalgamiento).

days.guide: Read 'Yo soy un hombre sincero' aloud twice; your child marks images of nature and the poet's identity, then listens to 'Guantanamera'.

questions.q: Where does the speaker say he comes from?
questions.a: 'De donde crece la palma' — from where the palm tree grows (Cuba).

questions.q: What does the speaker want to do before he dies?
questions.a: Share (echar) the verses of his soul — express his deepest feelings in poetry.

days.guide: Read Neruda's 'Oda al tomate'; your child lists metaphors and personifications and explains each in Spanish.

questions.q: How does Neruda treat an ordinary tomato in the ode?
questions.a: He celebrates it as something marvelous, personifying it and comparing it to a star or sun (an 'astro de tierra') that fills kitchens and summer meals.

questions.q: What is an 'oda'?
questions.a: A poem of praise addressed to a person or thing; Neruda's Odas elementales praise everyday objects.

days.guide: Read a Gabriela Mistral poem; discuss themes and learn that she was the first Latin American to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1945).

questions.q: Name two common themes in Mistral's poetry.
questions.a: Love for children and motherhood, nature, loss and grief, and her Chilean/Latin American identity.

days.guide: Your child writes an 'Oda a…' about an everyday object (calcetín, cuchara, mochila) using short lines and metaphors.

questions.q: Write two lines of an ode with a metaphor.
questions.a: Example: Oh, cuchara, / pequeña luna de metal.

days.guide: Your child recites the ode and one memorized stanza of Martí; score with the rubric.

questions.q: How many syllables are in each line of 'Yo soy un hombre sincero'?
questions.a: Eight (octosílabos).

weeks.assessment_key: Recital and ode rubric: Ode — 4 = 20+ short lines addressed to an everyday object, 4+ metaphors/similes, sensory images, accurate Spanish; 3 = fewer images or a few errors; 2 = list-like with errors; 1 = incomplete. Recital — 4 = memorized Martí stanza and ode delivered with clear pronunciation, pauses at punctuation, expression; 3 = minor slips; 2 = reads with hesitation; 1 = not prepared.

weeks.prep: Print Horacio Quiroga's 'El almohadón de plumas' (1907, public domain) with a glossary. Preview: a short horror story with a gradual illness, death, and a blood-drinking parasite. Chart the pluperfect: había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían + participle. Write the Unit 6 test (present perfect, pluperfect, art and literature vocabulary, a short reading).
misconceptions: Using the preterite where the pluperfect is needed: an action before another past action uses había + participle (Cuando llegué, la película ya había empezado).
Thinking the narrator explains everything early: Quiroga withholds the cause of Alicia's illness until the final paragraphs to create suspense.
Writing the summary in the present: the task asks for past tenses (preterite for events, imperfect for description).

days.guide: Teach the pluperfect with a timeline; your child writes 10 sentences about things that had already happened before a past moment.

questions.q: Translate: 'When I arrived, my brother had already eaten.'
questions.a: Cuando llegué, mi hermano ya había comido.

questions.q: Translate: 'They had never seen snow.'
questions.a: Nunca habían visto la nieve.

days.guide: Read 'El almohadón de plumas' aloud together with the glossary; stop after each section to check comprehension.

questions.q: Describe the house and the marriage at the start.
questions.a: The house is cold, white, and silent like an enchanted palace; Jordán is stern and undemonstrative, and Alicia, shy and timid, is unhappy and grows thin.

days.guide: Discuss how Quiroga builds suspense: the cold setting, Alicia's worsening illness, doctors who cannot explain it, and the hallucinations.

questions.q: What do the doctors find, and why can't they cure her?
questions.a: Severe anemia that worsens each day; they cannot explain the cause because it is hidden in the pillow.

questions.q: What is revealed at the end?
questions.a: A monstrous parasite inside the feather pillow had been sucking Alicia's blood every night through her temples.

days.guide: Your child writes a 200-word summary in past tenses using at least three pluperfect verbs.

questions.q: Write a sentence with the pluperfect about the story.
questions.a: Example: La sirvienta descubrió que el animal había chupado la sangre de Alicia.

days.guide: Give the Unit 6 test.

questions.q: Fill in: Alicia ya ___ (morir) cuando encontraron el parásito.
questions.a: había muerto

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 6 test sample key: 1) Cuando llegamos, el tren ya había salido 2) Ella nunca había visto un mural 3) he escrito / habían vuelto 4) Reading items: Alicia and Jordán are newlyweds; Alicia becomes weak and pale (anemia) and has hallucinations; she dies; the maid notices stains on the feather pillow; Jordán cuts it open and finds a swollen parasite that had been sucking Alicia's blood at night. Summary rubric (200 words): 4 = main events in order, correct preterite/imperfect/pluperfect, own words; 3 = minor errors; 2 = gaps or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find Spanish job ads (Computrabajo, InfoJobs, or LinkedIn en español) and a sample Spanish CV (currículum vitae/hoja de vida). Make career vocabulary cards (el/la abogado/a, el/la enfermero/a, el/la ingeniero/a, el/la contador/a, el sueldo, la jornada completa/parcial, los requisitos).
misconceptions: Using an article with professions after ser (*Soy un estudiante): Soy estudiante; Mi madre es enfermera (unless an adjective is added: Es una enfermera excelente).
False friends: 'la carrera' = career or college major; 'la lectura' = reading, not lecture; 'aplicar' is commonly heard but 'solicitar un puesto' is standard for applying to a job.

days.guide: Teach 20 career terms with masculine/feminine forms. Your child matches professions to descriptions.

questions.q: Translate: 'My aunt is an engineer.'
questions.a: Mi tía es ingeniera.

questions.q: Give the feminine of el abogado and el contador.
questions.a: la abogada; la contadora

days.guide: Your child reads three Spanish job ads and lists requirements, schedule, and salary for each.

questions.q: What does 'Se requiere experiencia mínima de dos años' mean?
questions.a: A minimum of two years of experience is required.

questions.q: What does 'Se ofrece' introduce in a job ad?
questions.a: What the employer offers (salary, benefits, schedule).

days.guide: Your child writes a one-page Spanish CV: datos personales, formación académica, experiencia, habilidades, idiomas.

questions.q: How do you say 'fluent in English, intermediate Spanish' on a CV?
questions.a: Inglés: nativo/fluido; español: nivel intermedio.

days.guide: Role-play a job interview: you are the interviewer (¿Por qué quiere trabajar aquí? ¿Cuáles son sus puntos fuertes?).

questions.q: Answer: 'Why do you want to work here?'
questions.a: Example: Quiero trabajar aquí porque me interesa ayudar a los clientes y soy responsable y puntual.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz and a final recorded interview.

questions.q: Ask politely: 'What is the salary?'
questions.a: ¿Cuál es el sueldo?

weeks.assessment_key: Interview rubric: 4 = uses usted throughout, answers 6+ questions with complete sentences about experience, skills, and availability, asks 2 questions; 3 = minor errors; 2 = short answers or tú/usted mixing; 1 = cannot sustain. Vocabulary quiz sample key: el sueldo = salary; la entrevista = interview; solicitar = to apply for; los requisitos = requirements; la experiencia laboral = work experience; jornada completa = full-time; el/la gerente = manager.

weeks.prep: Chart WEIRDO triggers for this week: emotion (alegrarse de que, me sorprende que, temer que, es una lástima que) and doubt/denial (dudar que, no creer que, no estar seguro de que, es posible que) vs. certainty (creer que, pensar que, estar seguro de que, es cierto que + indicative). Collect 10 current news headlines.
misconceptions: Using the subjunctive after creer que in affirmative statements (*Creo que sea verdad): Creo que es verdad; but No creo que sea verdad.
Using subjunctive with no change of subject: 'Me alegro de estar aquí' (same subject = infinitive) vs. 'Me alegro de que estés aquí'.
Forgetting 'de' in alegrarse de que.

days.guide: Teach emotion expressions + que + subjunctive. Your child writes 10 sentences about family news (Me alegro de que mi primo tenga trabajo).

questions.q: Translate: 'I'm glad that you are here.'
questions.a: Me alegro de que estés aquí.

questions.q: Translate: 'It surprises me that they don't know.'
questions.a: Me sorprende que no sepan.

days.guide: Contrast doubt/denial (subjunctive) with belief/certainty (indicative). Model pairs aloud.

questions.q: Choose: 'No creo que ella ___ (tener) razón' and 'Creo que ella ___ (tener) razón.'
questions.a: tenga; tiene

questions.q: Translate: 'I doubt that it will rain.'
questions.a: Dudo que llueva.

days.guide: Your child completes a mixed 20-item indicative/subjunctive exercise and writes the trigger next to each answer.

questions.q: Choose: 'Es verdad que el examen ___ (ser) mañana.'
questions.a: es (certainty → indicative)

questions.q: Choose: 'Es posible que nosotros ___ (ir) a la playa.'
questions.a: vayamos

days.guide: Your child reacts to 10 headlines using emotion and doubt expressions.

questions.q: React to 'Suben los precios de la gasolina' with an emotion expression.
questions.a: Example: Es una lástima que suban los precios de la gasolina.

days.guide: Give the quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Dudo que mi hermano está en casa.'
questions.a: Dudo que mi hermano esté en casa.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) Dudo que él venga 2) Creo que él viene 3) No creo que llueva hoy 4) Es posible que tengamos examen 5) Me alegro de que estés mejor 6) Es cierto que ella sabe la respuesta 7) Temo que no haya boletos 8) Pienso que es fácil / No pienso que sea fácil 9) Es una lástima que no puedas venir 10) Estoy seguro de que ganaremos.

weeks.prep: Find Spanish-language pages of nonprofits serving Spanish speakers in California (e.g., a local food bank, a legal aid group, the UFW Foundation) and a short Spanish reading on César Chávez and Dolores Huerta.
misconceptions: Thinking César Chávez founded the farmworker union alone: he co-founded the National Farm Workers Association (1962) with Dolores Huerta; it later became the United Farm Workers (UFW).
Writing proposals only in the present: use the future (Organizaremos...) and the subjunctive for goals (Queremos que los vecinos participen).

days.guide: Your child researches one nonprofit and records its mission, services, and whom it serves in Spanish.

questions.q: What does 'ONG' stand for?
questions.a: Organización no gubernamental — a non-governmental (nonprofit) organization.

days.guide: Read about Chávez, Huerta, and the UFW; your child makes a timeline of 5 events.

questions.q: What was the Delano grape strike?
questions.a: A strike by grape workers starting in 1965 in Delano, California, which grew into a nationwide consumer boycott of table grapes.

questions.q: What slogan is associated with Dolores Huerta?
questions.a: '¡Sí, se puede!' (Yes, it can be done).

days.guide: Discuss in Spanish: ¿Qué significa la comunidad para ti? ¿Cómo podemos ayudar?

questions.q: Translate: 'A community is a group of people who help each other.'
questions.a: Una comunidad es un grupo de personas que se ayudan mutuamente (unas a otras).

days.guide: Your child writes a proposal for a community project (problem, plan, materials, volunteers, expected results).

questions.q: Translate: 'We want the neighbors to participate.'
questions.a: Queremos que los vecinos participen.

days.guide: Your child presents the proposal for 3 minutes; score with the rubric.

questions.q: Translate: 'We will collect food every Saturday.'
questions.a: Recogeremos comida todos los sábados.

weeks.assessment_key: Proposal presentation rubric: 4 = identifies a real community need, describes the project with who/what/when/how, uses future and 3+ subjunctive structures, persuasive conclusion, 3 minutes; 3 = minor gaps or errors; 2 = vague plan or many errors; 1 = incomplete. Reading check key: Chávez and Huerta co-founded the NFWA in 1962; the Delano grape strike began in 1965 and led to a national grape boycott; nonviolent tactics (marches, fasts, boycotts); Huerta coined '¡Sí, se puede!' (1972).

weeks.prep: Chart adverbial clauses of time: cuando, tan pronto como, en cuanto, hasta que, después de que + subjunctive for future events; + indicative for habits or past events. Antes de que always takes the subjunctive. Write the Unit 7 test (careers, emotion/doubt subjunctive, adverbial clauses, community).
misconceptions: Using the future after cuando (*Cuando tendré 25 años): Cuando tenga 25 años, viviré en...
Using the subjunctive for habits: 'Cuando llego a casa, como' (habit = indicative).
Using 'después de que' with the same subject: use después de + infinitive (Después de graduarme, trabajaré).

days.guide: Teach the rule: pending/future action → subjunctive; habitual or completed → indicative. Your child completes 15 sentences.

questions.q: Translate: 'When I graduate, I will travel.'
questions.a: Cuando me gradúe, viajaré.

questions.q: Choose: 'Siempre como cuando ___ (llegar) a casa.'
questions.a: llego (habit → indicative)

days.guide: Your child writes a career plan with 10 sentences using the future and adverbial clauses.

questions.q: Translate: 'As soon as I have money, I will buy a car.'
questions.a: Tan pronto como tenga dinero, compraré un carro (coche).

days.guide: Your child records a 3-minute video 'Mi futuro'.

questions.q: Translate: 'I will work until I find my ideal job.'
questions.a: Trabajaré hasta que encuentre mi trabajo ideal.

days.guide: Give feedback on the video (content, grammar, pronunciation); your child revises and re-records weak parts.

questions.q: Correct: 'Después de que me graduaré, buscaré trabajo.'
questions.a: Después de que me gradúe, buscaré trabajo (or Después de graduarme, ...).

days.guide: Give the Unit 7 test.

questions.q: Fill in: Te llamaré en cuanto ___ (saber) los resultados.
questions.a: sepa

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 7 test sample key: 1) Cuando me gradúe, iré a la universidad 2) Tan pronto como llegues, llámame 3) Trabajaré hasta que tenga suficiente dinero 4) Cuando era niño, jugaba (past habit = indicative) 5) Antes de que salgas, cierra la puerta 6) Me alegro de que consigas el trabajo 7) No creo que sea fácil. Video rubric (3 minutes, 'Mi futuro'): 4 = clear career plan, 6+ future verbs, 4+ adverbial clauses with correct subjunctive, fluent; 3 = minor errors; 2 = short or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find a Spanish article on teens and social media in Spain (e.g., from El País, 20minutos, or a government INE/INJUVE survey summary). Prepare a family tech-use survey and graph paper or a spreadsheet.
misconceptions: Using English tech words with English grammar: Spanish verbs are often adapted (chatear, tuitear, descargar, subir una foto) and conjugated regularly.
Confusing 'la red' (network/the internet) and 'la red social' (a social network); 'la contraseña' = password, not 'el pase'.

days.guide: Teach 20 technology words; your child labels a screenshot of a phone and a computer.

questions.q: Translate: 'I downloaded an app and created a password.'
questions.a: Descargué una aplicación y creé una contraseña.

questions.q: What does 'subir una foto' mean?
questions.a: To upload (post) a photo.

days.guide: Your child surveys family members (¿Cuántas horas usas el celular al día? ¿Qué aplicación usas más?) and graphs results with Spanish labels.

questions.q: Report: 'Most of my family uses their phone three hours a day.'
questions.a: La mayoría de mi familia usa el celular tres horas al día.

days.guide: Read the article; your child summarizes the main statistics and the author's concern.

questions.q: What reading strategy helps with statistics in Spanish?
questions.a: Look for numbers with por ciento, la mitad, la mayoría, uno de cada… and note what each refers to; remember Spain writes decimals with commas (2,5 = 2.5).

days.guide: Debate: ¿Las redes sociales nos unen o nos separan? Your child argues one side, then the other.

questions.q: Give an argument that social networks unite us.
questions.a: Example: Las redes sociales nos unen porque podemos hablar con familiares que viven lejos.

days.guide: Give the vocabulary quiz and score the debate.

questions.q: Translate: 'Don't share your password.'
questions.a: No compartas tu contraseña.

weeks.assessment_key: Vocabulary quiz sample key: la red social = social network; descargar = to download; subir = to upload; la aplicación = app; la contraseña = password; el enlace = link; la pantalla = screen; el teclado = keyboard; guardar = to save; borrar = to delete. Debate rubric: 4 = clear position, 3 reasons with evidence, rebuttal, uses opinion phrases and subjunctive (No creo que..., Es importante que...); 3 = minor gaps; 2 = few reasons; 1 = cannot sustain.

weeks.prep: Chart conditional endings added to the whole infinitive (-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían) and the same irregular stems as the future (tendr-, saldr-, pondr-, vendr-, podr-, sabr-, querr-, habr-, har-, dir-). Write 10 '¿Qué harías?' scenario cards.
misconceptions: Regularizing irregular verbs (*hacería, *decería, *podería): the conditional uses the future's irregular stems — haría, diría, podría.
Translating every English 'would' as conditional: habitual past 'would' is imperfect (When I was little I would play outside = De pequeño jugaba afuera).
Forgetting accents: all conditional forms have an accent on the í.

days.guide: Teach formation and irregulars. Your child conjugates 15 verbs and says what they would do with a free day.

questions.q: Conjugate tener and venir in the conditional for yo.
questions.a: tendría; vendría

questions.q: Translate: 'We would travel to Peru.'
questions.a: Viajaríamos a Perú.

days.guide: Practice polite requests with the conditional (¿Podría...?, Me gustaría..., ¿Le importaría...?) in a restaurant and store role-play.

questions.q: Make polite: '¡Dame agua!'
questions.a: ¿Me podrías dar agua, por favor? (formal: ¿Me podría dar agua, por favor?)

days.guide: Your child answers 10 '¿Qué harías?' scenarios in full sentences.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué harías si encontraras una billetera en la calle?'
questions.a: Example: La llevaría a la policía (Buscaría al dueño).

days.guide: Your child describes an invention they would create: what it would do, who would use it, how much it would cost.

questions.q: Translate: 'My invention would clean the house by itself.'
questions.a: Mi invento limpiaría la casa solo.

days.guide: Give the conditional quiz.

questions.q: Correct: 'Yo hacería la tarea pero no podré.'
questions.a: Yo haría la tarea, pero no podría (or no puedo).

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) hablar/yo — hablaría 2) comer/tú — comerías 3) tener/él — tendría 4) salir/nosotros — saldríamos 5) hacer/ellos — harían 6) decir/yo — diría 7) poder/ustedes — podrían 8) poner/tú — pondrías 9) 'Could you help me?' — ¿Podría ayudarme? / ¿Podrías ayudarme? 10) 'I would like a coffee' — Me gustaría (Quisiera) un café.

weeks.prep: Bookmark BBC Mundo (bbc.com/mundo) and Univision Noticias; choose two short articles and three Spanish-language ads. Prepare a fake-news checklist (fuente, fecha, autor, otras fuentes, titular exagerado).
misconceptions: Believing a headline without reading the article: check the source, date, author, and whether other reliable outlets report it.
Confusing 'la noticia' (one news item) and 'las noticias' (the news); 'el noticiero' is the newscast.
