days.guide: Your child reads two BBC Mundo articles and summarizes each in 5 Spanish sentences (qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, por qué).

questions.q: What does 'el titular' mean?
questions.a: The headline.

days.guide: Your child analyzes three ads for persuasive techniques (emotion, humor, famous people, statistics, imperatives).

questions.q: Identify the technique: '¡Compra ya! Solo por hoy.'
questions.a: Urgency/scarcity with a command.

days.guide: Teach a fake-news checklist; your child evaluates two headlines (one real, one invented by you).

questions.q: Name three ways to check if a news story is fake.
questions.a: Check the source and author, check the date, and see if other reliable outlets report it (also look for exaggerated headlines and errors).

days.guide: Your child scripts and records a 2-minute newscast with three stories.

questions.q: Write an anchor's opening line.
questions.a: Example: Buenas noches. Les habla (nombre) con las noticias más importantes del día.

days.guide: Your child presents the newscast; score with the rubric.

questions.q: Translate: 'The mayor said that the park will open on Monday.'
questions.a: El alcalde dijo que el parque abrirá (abriría) el lunes.

weeks.assessment_key: Newscast rubric (2 minutes): 4 = 3 stories with who/what/when/where, past tenses and reported speech, clear anchor phrases (Buenas noches, les informamos que..., En otras noticias...), clear delivery; 3 = minor errors; 2 = short or unclear; 1 = incomplete. Reading summaries checked for main idea and three accurate details from each article.

weeks.prep: Chart the imperfect subjunctive: take the ellos preterite, drop -ron, add -ra, -ras, -ra, -'ramos, -rais, -ran (hablaran → hablara; tuvieron → tuviera; fueron → fuera). Choose a song with si clauses and print the lyrics (use only the portion you need). Write the Unit 8 test (technology, conditional, media, imperfect subjunctive, si clauses).
misconceptions: Using the conditional in the si clause (*Si tendría dinero): Si tuviera dinero, viajaría.
Missing the accent on the nosotros form: habláramos, tuviéramos, fuéramos.
Mixing types: si + present → present/future/command (real); si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional (hypothetical).

days.guide: Teach formation from the ellos preterite; your child conjugates 20 verbs.

questions.q: Give the imperfect subjunctive yo form of hablar, tener, hacer, and ir.
questions.a: hablara, tuviera, hiciera, fuera

questions.q: Give the nosotros form of estar.
questions.a: estuviéramos

days.guide: Teach si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional; your child writes 10 'Si yo fuera…' sentences.

questions.q: Translate: 'If I were rich, I would buy a house for my parents.'
questions.a: Si yo fuera rico/a, compraría una casa para mis padres.

questions.q: Translate: 'If I had a dog, I would walk it every day.'
questions.a: Si tuviera un perro, lo pasearía todos los días.

days.guide: Listen to a song with si clauses; your child highlights each si clause in the lyrics and explains whether it is real or hypothetical.

questions.q: How do you tell a real si clause from a hypothetical one?
questions.a: Real: si + present indicative (Si puedo, voy). Hypothetical/contrary to fact: si + imperfect subjunctive with the conditional (Si pudiera, iría).

days.guide: Your child writes 'Si pudiera cambiar el mundo…' (200 words).

questions.q: Write an opening sentence.
questions.a: Example: Si pudiera cambiar el mundo, eliminaría el hambre y daría educación a todos los niños.

days.guide: Give the Unit 8 test.

questions.q: Correct: 'Si yo tendría alas, volaré.'
questions.a: Si yo tuviera alas, volaría.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 8 test sample key: 1) tener/yo — tuviera 2) ser/ir/ellos — fueran 3) poder/nosotros — pudiéramos 4) decir/tú — dijeras 5) Si yo fuera presidente, cambiaría las leyes 6) Si tuviéramos tiempo, iríamos al cine 7) Si llueve mañana, me quedaré en casa 8) ¿Qué harías si ganaras la lotería? 9) media vocabulary: el titular, el noticiero, la noticia falsa. Essay rubric (200 words, 'Si pudiera cambiar el mundo…'): 4 = 6+ correct si clauses, clear ideas, varied vocabulary; 3 = minor errors; 2 = few si clauses or many errors; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find short videos (Smithsonian, National Geographic en español, tourism boards) on Día de los Muertos, Las Fallas (Valencia, Spain), and Inti Raymi (Cusco, Peru). Choose a pan de muerto or tamales recipe in Spanish and buy ingredients.
misconceptions: Calling Día de los Muertos 'Mexican Halloween': it is a family celebration on November 1–2 honoring and welcoming the spirits of loved ones, rooted in Indigenous and Catholic traditions.
Thinking Inti Raymi is in December: it is held June 24 in Cusco, near the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice, honoring Inti, the Inca sun god.

days.guide: Read about Día de los Muertos; your child labels an ofrenda diagram explaining each item in Spanish.

questions.q: Why are marigolds (cempasúchil) placed on the ofrenda?
questions.a: Their bright color and strong scent are believed to guide the spirits to the altar.

questions.q: Translate: 'We put photos of our grandparents on the altar.'
questions.a: Ponemos fotos de nuestros abuelos en el altar (la ofrenda).

days.guide: Watch videos on Las Fallas and Inti Raymi; your child takes notes (where, when, what happens, meaning).

questions.q: What happens at the end of Las Fallas?
questions.a: On the night of March 19 (la Cremà) the giant figures are burned.

questions.q: What does Inti Raymi celebrate?
questions.a: Inti, the Inca sun god, at the winter solstice and the start of the new year in the Andes.

days.guide: Your child compares one Hispanic celebration with a family celebration using comparison phrases (al igual que, a diferencia de, mientras que).

questions.q: Write a comparison sentence.
questions.a: Example: Al igual que el Día de Acción de Gracias, el Día de Muertos reúne a la familia, pero a diferencia de él, se recuerda a los muertos.

days.guide: Follow a Spanish recipe together; your child narrates the steps with commands or se (Se mezcla la harina...).

questions.q: Translate the step: 'Mix the flour with the eggs.'
questions.a: Mezcla la harina con los huevos (Se mezcla la harina con los huevos).

days.guide: Give the festivals quiz.

questions.q: When and where is Inti Raymi celebrated?
questions.a: June 24 in Cusco, Peru.

weeks.assessment_key: Quiz sample key: 1) Día de los Muertos — Nov. 1–2, Mexico; ofrendas honor deceased relatives 2) el cempasúchil (marigold) — its color and scent guide the spirits 3) las velas — light the way 4) el agua — quenches the spirits' thirst after the journey 5) el pan de muerto — offering of food 6) Las Fallas — Valencia, March, giant figures (ninots/fallas) burned on the night of March 19 (San José) 7) Inti Raymi — June 24, Cusco, Festival of the Sun 8) la quinceañera — a girl's 15th birthday celebration marking the passage to young womanhood.

weeks.prep: Find readings on mestizaje and Afro-Latino culture (e.g., Smithsonian or BBC Mundo articles), and audio of cumbia, salsa, and son jarocho. List borrowed words: Nahuatl (chocolate, tomate, aguacate, chicle, cacahuate), Quechua (papa, cóndor, llama, puma, pampa), Arabic (almohada, azúcar, aceite, arroz, ojalá, alcalde, ajedrez).
misconceptions: Thinking Latin American culture is only Spanish and Indigenous: millions of enslaved Africans were brought to the Americas, and African heritage is central in the Caribbean, Colombia, Venezuela, Peru, Brazil, and beyond.
Using 'raza' or racial labels casually: discuss identity terms respectfully (afrodescendiente, indígena, mestizo) and note that people self-identify in different ways.

days.guide: Read about mestizaje; your child makes a three-column chart of Indigenous, African, and European influences.

questions.q: Give one example of each influence in Latin American food.
questions.a: Indigenous: maíz, chocolate, papa; African: mofongo (from West African fufu), plantain dishes, okra (quimbombó); European: wheat bread, pork, olive oil.

days.guide: Listen to cumbia, salsa, and son jarocho; your child identifies instruments and their origins.

questions.q: Where does cumbia come from, and what are its roots?
questions.a: Colombia's Caribbean coast; it blends African drums, Indigenous flutes (gaitas) and maracas, and European influences.

questions.q: Where is son jarocho from, and what instrument is typical?
questions.a: Veracruz, Mexico; the jarana (a small guitar), along with the requinto and harp, and zapateado dancing on a wooden platform (tarima).

days.guide: Your child learns borrowed words and sorts them by language of origin.

questions.q: Which language gave Spanish 'chocolate' and 'aguacate'? Which gave 'almohada' and 'ojalá'?
questions.a: Nahuatl; Arabic.

days.guide: Discuss sincretismo in celebrations (Día de Muertos, la Virgen de Guadalupe, Santería) in Spanish.

questions.q: What is 'sincretismo'?
questions.a: The blending of different religious or cultural traditions into a new practice, such as Indigenous ancestor honoring combined with Catholic All Souls' Day in Día de Muertos.

days.guide: Your child writes a 250-word reflective essay.

questions.q: Translate: 'Latin American culture is a mix of many traditions.'
questions.a: La cultura latinoamericana es una mezcla de muchas tradiciones.

weeks.assessment_key: Essay rubric (250 words, reflective): 4 = explains indigenous, African, and European influences with 3 specific examples (music, language, food, religion), personal reflection, varied past and subjunctive structures, accurate; 3 = minor gaps or errors; 2 = general with few examples; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Find Pew Research Center or U.S. Census data on Latinos in California (Latinos are about 40% of the state's population, the largest ethnic group). Arrange an interview with a Spanish speaker (in person or video). Locate a local Spanish-language radio station online. Write the Unit 9 test (festivals, heritage, Latino culture in the U.S., subjunctive review).
misconceptions: Assuming all Latinos speak Spanish or share one culture: Latinos in the U.S. have roots in many countries, and many are English-dominant or bilingual.
Treating Spanglish as 'bad Spanish': code-switching is a normal skill of bilingual speakers; formal writing still uses standard Spanish.

days.guide: Your child analyzes data on the Latino population in California and writes 5 findings in Spanish.

questions.q: Translate: 'About forty percent of Californians are Latino.'
questions.a: Aproximadamente el cuarenta por ciento de los californianos son latinos.

days.guide: Your child interviews a Spanish speaker with 10 questions (origin, arrival, work, traditions, language) and records it with permission.

questions.q: Ask: 'How long have you lived in California?'
questions.a: ¿Cuánto tiempo hace que vive en California? (¿Desde hace cuánto vive en California?)

days.guide: Listen to a local Spanish-language radio segment; your child summarizes the topic and 3 details.

questions.q: What is 'el bilingüismo'?
questions.a: Bilingualism — speaking two languages.

days.guide: Your child writes a report on the interview with quotations and reported speech.

questions.q: Convert to reported speech: 'Me encanta mi comunidad,' dijo la señora.
questions.a: La señora dijo que le encantaba su comunidad.

days.guide: Give the Unit 9 test.

questions.q: Fill in: Es importante que los jóvenes ___ (mantener) el español.
questions.a: mantengan

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 9 test sample key: 1) Latinos ≈ 40% of Californians, the largest group 2) el bilingüismo = bilingualism 3) el spanglish = mixing Spanish and English 4) festival items (Día de Muertos, Fallas, Inti Raymi) 5) borrowed words: Nahuatl/Quechua/Arabic examples 6) subjunctive: Es importante que mantengamos el idioma; Si viviera en México, hablaría español todos los días. Report rubric: 4 = summarizes the interviewee's background, work, and traditions with accurate past tenses and direct quotations, plus a reflection; 3 = minor errors; 2 = thin; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: Help your child choose a project format (documentary, magazine, or podcast on a Spanish-speaking country) and find three authentic Spanish sources (news sites, tourism boards, government or museum pages). Print a grammar revision checklist (preterite/imperfect, subjunctive triggers, agreement, accents).
misconceptions: Translating an English draft word by word: write directly in Spanish with known structures and check new expressions in a dictionary like SpanishDict or WordReference.
Citing sources incorrectly: name the source in Spanish (Según BBC Mundo..., De acuerdo con...).

days.guide: Your child chooses a format and country and writes a one-paragraph plan in Spanish.

questions.q: Translate: 'My podcast will be about the history and food of Peru.'
questions.a: Mi pódcast será sobre la historia y la comida de Perú.

days.guide: Your child researches using three authentic sources and takes notes in Spanish (no copied sentences).

questions.q: How do you introduce information from a source in Spanish?
questions.a: Según (la fuente)..., De acuerdo con..., El artículo de ... explica que...

days.guide: Your child writes the script or articles (600+ words) with introduction, sections, and conclusion.

questions.q: Write a transition to a new section.
questions.a: Example: Ahora, hablemos de la comida típica del país.

days.guide: Your child revises with the checklist; you mark errors with codes (T = tense, S = subjunctive, A = agreement, Ac = accent) for self-correction.

questions.q: Correct: 'Es necesario que los turistas visitan la ciudad antigua.'
questions.a: Es necesario que los turistas visiten la ciudad antigua.

days.guide: Your child rehearses the presentation once with you, timing it.

questions.q: Write a closing line.
questions.a: Example: Gracias por escuchar. ¡Espero que algún día puedan visitar este país maravilloso!

weeks.assessment_key: Checkpoint rubric: 4 = topic approved, three authentic sources cited, 600+ word script/articles drafted, revised with the checklist, rehearsed once; 3 = one element incomplete; 2 = two incomplete; 1 = not started.

weeks.prep: Set up recording or layout tools for the final product and a quiet space for the presentation. Print the project rubric and a portfolio checklist (best writing, recordings, tests, the art label, the legend, the newscast).
misconceptions: Reading the script word for word during the presentation: use notes and speak to the audience.
Giving only praise in feedback: give one specific strength and one specific suggestion in Spanish.

days.guide: Your child produces the final video, podcast, or magazine.

questions.q: Translate: 'I edited the video and added music.'
questions.a: Edité el video y añadí (agregué) música.

days.guide: Your child presents the project and answers three questions in Spanish.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Por qué elegiste este país?'
questions.a: Example: Elegí este país porque mi familia es de allí y quería aprender más sobre su historia.

days.guide: Your child watches a sibling's or online student's project and gives feedback in Spanish.

questions.q: Give a suggestion politely in Spanish.
questions.a: Example: Me gustó mucho tu introducción; te sugiero que hables un poco más despacio.

days.guide: Your child writes a reflection on the year's learning.

questions.q: Translate: 'At the beginning of the year I couldn't use the subjunctive, but now I can.'
questions.a: Al principio del año no podía usar el subjuntivo, pero ahora sí puedo.

days.guide: Your child organizes the portfolio of the year's best work with labels in Spanish.

questions.q: What should a portfolio entry include?
questions.a: The work, the date, and a short note in Spanish on what skill it shows (e.g., Este ensayo muestra mi uso del subjuntivo).

weeks.assessment_key: Project rubric: 4 = content accurate and well organized with three sources, varied tenses including subjunctive and si clauses with few errors, clear pronunciation, answers 3 questions in Spanish, polished production; 3 = minor issues in one area; 2 = issues in several areas; 1 = incomplete. Reflection: 4 = 200+ words comparing early and current skills with examples and goals.

weeks.prep: Assemble the final review packet and exam: an authentic article and podcast clip with questions, a 300-word essay prompt (e.g., ¿Cómo ha cambiado tu identidad como estudiante de español?), and an oral interview question list. Help your child choose a summer book or series in Spanish (e.g., a graded reader or a show such as a Spanish-language series with subtitles).
misconceptions: Using only present tense in the oral interview: push for past, future, conditional, and subjunctive with follow-up questions (¿Qué hiciste...? ¿Qué harías si...?).
Rushing the essay without planning: outline thesis, three points, and conclusion first.

days.guide: Your child reviews all tenses and moods with a mixed set and corrects errors.

questions.q: Give: preterite yo of hacer, imperfect yo of ver, present perfect yo of escribir, conditional yo of poder, imperfect subjunctive yo of ser.
questions.a: hice, veía, he escrito, podría, fuera

days.guide: Give the interpretive section: an authentic article and a podcast clip with questions.

questions.q: What should you do first with an authentic text?
questions.a: Read the title, subtitles, and questions, predict the topic, then read for gist before details.

days.guide: Give the writing section: a 300-word essay.

questions.q: Translate a thesis: 'Learning Spanish has changed how I see the world.'
questions.a: Aprender español ha cambiado mi manera de ver el mundo.

days.guide: Hold a 10-minute oral proficiency interview: warm-up, questions in several tenses, a role-play, and a wind-down.

questions.q: Answer: '¿Qué harías si pudieras vivir en otro país?'
questions.a: Example: Si pudiera vivir en otro país, viviría en Argentina porque me encantaría aprender a bailar tango.

days.guide: Your child sets Spanish IV goals and chooses a summer book or series in Spanish.

questions.q: Translate: 'This summer I will read a book in Spanish.'
questions.a: Este verano leeré un libro en español.

weeks.assessment_key: Final exam: interpretive items keyed to the chosen article and podcast (main idea, 3 details, author's purpose, vocabulary in context). Essay rubric (300 words): 4 = clear thesis, organized paragraphs with transitions (además, sin embargo, por lo tanto), accurate use of at least 4 tenses/moods; 3 = minor errors; 2 = weak organization or frequent errors; 1 = incomplete. Oral proficiency interview (10 minutes): 4 = Intermediate Mid — creates with language, connected sentences, asks and answers questions, handles past/future/hypothetical with some errors; 3 = Intermediate Low; 2 = Novice High; 1 = memorized phrases only.
